title: Medigap Guaranteed Issue and Medicare Advantage

sections.text: Why Switching Back to Original Medicare Isn't Always Simple

sections.content: You can leave a Medicare Advantage plan and return to Original Medicare during certain enrollment windows, but getting a Medigap policy approved is a separate matter entirely. Enrollment timing and medical underwriting operate by different rules, and conflating the two is one of the most common and costly misunderstandings in Medicare.

Many people assume Medicare functions like other insurance they have had, where switching plans does not involve a health review. Medigap does not always work that way. Outside of specific protected periods, an insurer can ask about your health history before deciding whether to sell you a policy, and at what price.

This gap between when you are allowed to switch and when an insurer must accept you is exactly what leaves some beneficiaries stuck in a Medicare Advantage plan that no longer matches their doctors, budget, or health needs.

sections.text: What 'Guaranteed Issue' Actually Means for Your Medigap Rights

sections.content: Guaranteed issue is a federal protection that requires a Medigap insurer to sell you a policy regardless of your health history. During a guaranteed issue period, the insurer cannot deny you coverage, charge you more because of a medical condition, or make you wait for a pre-existing condition to be covered.

These rights are not permanent or ongoing. They apply only during specific triggering events defined under federal law, most notably the six-month period that starts the month you are both 65 or older and enrolled in Medicare Part B.

sections.calloutText: Your initial Medigap guaranteed issue period runs for six months starting the month you turn 65 or older and are enrolled in Part B. Outside this window and a few other qualifying events, insurers in most states can use medical underwriting.

items: You move outside your Medicare Advantage plan's service area
Your Medicare Advantage plan leaves the Medicare program or ends its contract with Medicare
You joined Medicare Advantage when you first became eligible for Medicare and want to switch within your first 12 months (a trial right)

sections.content: Outside these windows and a short list of other qualifying events, an insurer can ask health questions on your application and decide whether to approve you, decline you, or approve you at a higher premium based on your medical history. You can review the full list of protected situations on the [Medicare guaranteed issue rights page](https://www.medicare.gov/).

sections.text: The Medigap Gap: Why Many Beneficiaries Get Stuck

sections.content: Here is where the trap often forms. If you enrolled in Medicare Advantage at 65 and are happy with it for several years, you may eventually want to switch to Original Medicare paired with a Medigap policy, perhaps because your health needs changed or you want more flexibility in choosing providers. By that point, you have typically used up your federal guaranteed issue window.

In most states, that means the Medigap insurer can require you to answer health questions. Conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, cancer history, or other chronic illnesses can lead to a denial or a significantly higher premium offer, even though your Medicare Advantage plan never asked about your health when you enrolled.

This creates a real financial and health risk for people who chose Medicare Advantage at 65 without realizing that returning to Medigap later is not guaranteed. The decision you make in your first year of Medicare eligibility can shape your options for the rest of your time on Medicare.

sections.text: Do Any States Offer Broader Medigap Protections?

sections.content: Federal law sets the minimum guaranteed issue protections, but states are free to expand on them. A small number of states require insurers to offer Medigap policies with continuous or annual guaranteed issue rights, meaning residents are not limited to the narrow federal triggering events.

New York and Connecticut, for example, require continuous or year-round guaranteed issue access to Medigap policies for eligible residents. Massachusetts and Maine have also adopted expanded consumer protections that give residents more flexibility to switch between Medicare Advantage and Medigap without a full medical underwriting review. Rules and the specific plans affected vary by state, so always confirm current requirements with your state insurance department.

Even in states with broader protections, plan availability and pricing still vary by insurer. A state-level guarantee that you can get a policy does not mean every company offers the same premium, so comparing carriers remains worthwhile.

sections.text: How to Check Your Options Before the Annual Enrollment Period Ends

sections.content: Before you decide to leave Medicare Advantage, a few concrete checks can prevent you from ending up without coverage you can afford.

items: Review your specific state's Medigap rules, since protections for switching outside federal guaranteed issue windows differ significantly from one state to another.
Gather your health history, including current diagnoses, medications, and recent hospitalizations, so you understand how a Medigap insurer's underwriting questions might apply to you.

Compare your current Medicare Advantage costs and coverage, including your copays, provider network, and out-of-pocket maximum, against what Original Medicare plus a Medigap policy and a Part D plan would cost for your situation.
Confirm your Medigap application has been approved before you cancel or disenroll from your Medicare Advantage plan.

sections.calloutText: Dropping your Medicare Advantage plan before a Medigap insurer approves your application can leave you with no supplemental coverage and limited ability to rejoin Medicare Advantage until the next enrollment period.

sections.content: If you are even considering a future switch away from Medicare Advantage, apply for Medigap before you cancel anything. Keep your Medicare Advantage coverage active while your Medigap application is under review, and only disenroll once you have written confirmation of approval. This single sequencing decision is what separates a smooth transition from a coverage gap.

sections.text: Steps to Take if You're Denied Medigap Coverage

sections.content: A denial is not necessarily the end of the road. A few practical steps can help you understand your options and move forward.

items: Ask the insurer for the specific medical reason behind the denial, and whether a modified premium or alternate plan letter is available instead of a flat rejection.
Explore other Medigap carriers, since underwriting standards, accepted conditions, and premium rate-ups are not identical from one insurance company to another.
Consider staying on your current Medicare Advantage plan for another year while you plan for a future guaranteed issue event, such as a plan contract termination or a move outside your service area.

Talk with a licensed Medicare agent who can review multiple carriers' underwriting guidelines on your behalf, which can save you from applying to companies unlikely to approve your specific health history.

sections.text: Getting Clear, Pressure-Free Guidance on Your Next Step

sections.content: You do not need to work through this decision alone, and you do not need to rush it before you feel ready. Understanding guaranteed issue timing, state rules, and underwriting outcomes involves more moving pieces than most people want to track on their own.

A licensed Medicare agent can walk through your health history, your current doctors, and your budget to show you what is realistic given your state's specific rules. The goal of that conversation is a clear side-by-side comparison, not a push toward any particular plan.

sections.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Medigap and Medicare Advantage

faqs.question: Can I take my time deciding without losing my options?
faqs.answer: You can take time to review your situation, but specific deadlines still matter, such as the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7 for switching plans, and any guaranteed issue window you may be in. Reviewing calmly now, before a deadline is close, helps you avoid a rushed decision later.

faqs.question: Will I be pressured into a decision if I ask for help?
faqs.answer: A licensed agent's role is to explain your options clearly, not to push you toward a sale. You control the pace of the conversation, and you can ask questions, request time to think, or revisit the discussion later without obligation.

faqs.question: Can I just research this myself before talking to anyone?
faqs.answer: Researching on your own is a reasonable first step, and understanding the basics helps you ask better questions later. However, state-specific Medigap rules, underwriting nuances between carriers, and how your particular health history might be evaluated are details that often get missed without a personalized review.

faqs.question: How do I know which source of Medicare information to trust?
faqs.answer: Look for transparency about licensing, which states and carriers an agent or source actually represents, and clear explanations rather than vague promises. Credible sources explain tradeoffs honestly, disclose how guidance is provided, and are willing to answer specific questions about your situation rather than steering you toward one option.

sections.text: Making a Confident Choice About Your Coverage

sections.content: Understanding how guaranteed issue timing works protects you from being locked into a Medicare Advantage plan that no longer fits your doctors, prescriptions, or health needs. The earlier you understand these rules, the more control you have over your future options.

Reviewing your state's specific Medigap protections and your own health history before a deadline approaches gives you time to make a sound decision rather than a hurried one. A brief, no-pressure conversation with a licensed agent can clarify whether switching to Original Medicare and Medigap makes sense for your circumstances, or whether staying on Medicare Advantage remains the better fit for now.

seoTitle: Medigap Guaranteed Issue and Medicare Advantage
seoDescription: Learn how Medigap guaranteed issue Medicare Advantage rules can trap you in a plan and limit your options to switch later.
excerpt: Switching from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare does not guarantee you can get a Medigap policy. Without guaranteed issue rights, insurers can deny coverage based on health history.
keyTakeaways: Guaranteed issue rights force Medigap insurers to accept you regardless of health history, but these rights apply only during specific protected periods
Your initial Medigap guaranteed issue period lasts six months starting the month you turn 65 and enroll in Part B
Once this window closes, insurers in most states can use medical underwriting to deny coverage or charge higher premiums
Switching from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare does not automatically restore your Medigap guaranteed issue rights
Conditions like diabetes, heart disease, or cancer history can lead to denial or higher premiums if you apply for Medigap outside a guaranteed issue period
